extracted.intended_audience: newsrooms, websites, bloggers and broadcasters who want to republish Texas Tribune content
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for republishing The Texas Tribune's stories, photos, graphics, video and other multimedia online or on-air, including attribution, permissible edits, metadata, licensing, and commercial restrictions. Covers both text-story and multimedia-specific rules and contact points for permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline credit format (stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must give us credit, ideally in this format: “by Patrick Svitek, The Texas Tribune.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribution should be given prominently. The page gives the ideal wording as the example; contact press@texastribune.org for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include original story links (stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you publish online, you must include the links from the story, and a link to texastribune.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Republished online stories should preserve the hyperlinks that appeared in the original and include a link back to the Tribune's site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible style edits (stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: It's fine to change the story to suit your in-house style (for example, using “Beaumont, Tex.” instead of “Beaumont.”)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor, stylistic changes are allowed without additional attribution; more substantive changes require following the 'significant changes' rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical URL metadata (stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you publish online, when possible, include the Texas Tribune URL of the story as the value of the canonical tag in the metadata (<head>) of your republished story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps search engines recognize the Tribune as the original source. Implement as the canonical link element in the page head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution for significant edits or added reporting (stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you make changes that are more significant than style tweaks — such as adding a comment from a local official — you need to include a note like this: “Additional reporting by the Rosebud Reporter.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear note indicating additional reporting/contributions whenever content beyond stylistic edits is added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo/graphics republishing tied to original story
rubrics_metrics.description: You can publish our photos and graphics with the stories with which they originally appeared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For photo licensing questions, email licensing@texastribune.org. For uses outside the original story context, seek licensing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include organizational tagline when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, include the following: The Texas Tribune is a nonprofit, nonpartisan media organization that informs Texans — and engages with them — about public policy, politics, government and statewide issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This suggested blurb is optional ('when possible') but recommended to convey the Tribune's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media credit (stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you share the story on social media, please mention @TexasTribune (Twitter and Facebook) and @Texas_Tribune (Instagram).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tagging the Tribune on the relevant platforms is requested when reposting to social networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not sell the story (stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t sell the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Republished content must not be sold as a product or behind a paywall as a standalone item in a way that amounts to selling the story itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ads restriction against republished story (stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t sell ads against the story. Feel free, however, to publish it on a page surrounded by ads you’ve already sold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may display pre-existing page-level advertising, but you may not sell ad placements specifically against the republished Tribune story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracker pixel disclosure (stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles include a pixel to help us measure the reach and understand the impact of our stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tracker captures view counts and breaks them down by date, your site’s domain and from where you grabbed the article. No other information is gathered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party partner content exception
rubrics_metrics.description: From time to time, The Texas Tribune publishes content written by other newsrooms as part of exclusive partnerships. Stories written by third-party partners are not available for republishing, unlike regular Texas Tribune stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether a story is produced by a third-party partner before republishing; those items are excluded from these republishing permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline/credit format for multimedia and on-air use
rubrics_metrics.description: You must give us credit, ideally in this format: “by Patrick Svitek, The Texas Tribune.” For on-air use, please introduce video packages as “(Reporter) with our political reporting partner, The Texas Tribune…”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For shortened or re-aired packages, include the recommended verbal or visual credit; contact multimedia@texastribune.org with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include original story links (multimedia)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you publish online, you must include the links from the story, and a link to texastribune.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same requirement as for stories: preserve links and include a link back when republishing multimedia online.

rubrics_metrics.name: No alteration of video/audio without approval
rubrics_metrics.description: For multimedia, you can’t change video or audio packages in any way (included shortening) without receiving clear approval from Tribune editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to shorten or alter content in a hurry, email multimedia@texastribune.org. If granted approval to shorten for use as an anchor voice-over (VOSOT), provide a verbal or visual courtesy credit (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution for significant edits or added reporting (multimedia)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you make changes that are more significant than style tweaks — such as adding a comment from a local official — you need to include a note like this: “Additional reporting by the Rosebud Reporter.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same standard as stories: substantive additions to multimedia items require a clear note indicating additional reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia copyright/permission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: You can publish our multimedia pieces with the stories with which they originally appeared. For any other uses, you must seek permission from our multimedia department, multimedia@texastribune.org, as we do not always have the copyrights to pass along.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume multimedia may be republished independently of its original story without explicit permission from the multimedia department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include organizational tagline when possible (multimedia)
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, include the following: The Texas Tribune is a nonprofit, nonpartisan media organization that informs Texans — and engages with them — about public policy, politics, government and statewide issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the same suggested blurb recommended for story republishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media credit (multimedia)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you share the story on social media, please mention @TexasTribune (Twitter and Facebook) and @Texas_Tribune (Instagram).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request repeated for multimedia shares as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not sell the multimedia piece
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t sell the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimedia content republished under these guidelines must not be sold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ads restriction against republished multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t sell ads against the story. Feel free, however, to publish it on a page surrounded by ads you’ve already sold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same nuance as story ads restriction: pre-existing page ads okay, selling ad placements specifically against the republished content is not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with change/remove requests (multimedia)
rubrics_metrics.description: If we send you a request to change or remove Tribune content from your site or on-air, you must agree to do so immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribune may request edits or removal; republishers must promptly comply. Contact multimedia@texastribune.org for questions.
